query: /bruhs:cook move fleet balance reads off the primary db; the dashboard and the billing service both read them
context: Balance reads hit the primary on every dashboard load; p95 went from 100 ms to 600 ms over six months as the table grew past 40M rows. Two teams consume balances. Options: read replica, cache with invalidation on write, or a materialized balances table. The repo keeps design docs in docs/design/.
expected_behavior: Recognizes the design-doc triggers (another team depends on it, hard-to-reverse storage choice, unclear design) and writes a doc before building
Saves the doc under docs/design/ following the existing file naming
The doc stays within about three pages, with implementer-only detail in a collapsed appendix
The problem section states the evidence with numbers (100 ms to 600 ms, 40M rows), who is hurt, and why now, without proposing a solution
Goals are measurable outcomes (for example a p95 target at a load multiple), and non-goals are listed
Includes one mermaid diagram with a title, named boxes, and every arrow labelled with its intent, highlighting what changes
Alternatives are a short table of the options with one-line reasons
Risks and rollout list only the concerns that apply, such as cache staleness for billing and rollback
Runs the cold-read gate with a fresh subagent and fixes what it misses, then asks the user to approve the doc before implementing
failure_modes: Writes an implementation manual (file-by-file steps) with no trade-offs or alternatives
Opens with the solution ('we will add Redis') instead of the problem
Pads the doc with boilerplate sections marked N/A
Draws a diagram with unlabelled arrows or arrows labelled 'uses'
Starts coding before the doc is approved
